messages.author: 0152f60f8ff48c01
messages.subject: knitr and UTF-8
parts:
Dear list,

some days ago I installed knitr. Unfortunately, I can not figure out
how to 'knit' a document encoded in UTF-8:

Code Chunk:

<<>>=
bsp <- read.csv("data/Sympathie.csv")
fit <- lm(Sympathie ~ Redefluss + Attraktivität, data = bsp)
summary(fit)
@

Error:

> knit("GLM.Rnw")
...
Unable to parse the R code! The error most likely came from line 2;
the surrounding lines are:
########################################################
bsp <- read.csv("data/Sympathie.csv")
fit <- lm(Sympathie ~ Redefluss + Attraktivität, data = bsp)
summary(fit)
########################################################
See the reference in help(tidy.source) for possible reasons

Warning in block_exec(params) :
failed to tidy R code in chunk <unnamed-chunk-1>
reason: Error in tidy.source(text = code, output = FALSE) :
Error in parser(text = text.lines) :
/tmp/Rtmpkg11GR/file2513415eaa03:2:45
unexpected input

When commenting lm and summary lines , knit() works. Sweave with
option encoding="UTF-8" works perfectly.

Outout from sessionInfo():

R version 2.15.0 (2012-03-30)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)

locale:
[1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C
[3] LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8 LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8
[5] LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8
[7] LC_PAPER=C LC_NAME=C
[9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C
[11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

attached base packages:
[1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods
base

other attached packages:
[1] knitr_0.4

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
[1] codetools_0.2-8 digest_0.5.2 evaluate_0.4.2 formatR_0.4
[5] highlight_0.3.1 parser_0.0-14 plyr_1.7.1 Rcpp_0.9.10
[9] stringr_0.6 tools_2.15.0
>

Any Ideas?

Thanks, Sven

BTW. help(tidy.source) does not work for me.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr and UTF-8
parts:
That is a problem of the parser package; it seems to be unable to
parse R tokens which are not regular names (e.g. not alphanumeric). In
this case, Attraktivität cannot be processed by parser.

library(parser)
parser(text = 'fit <- lm(Sympathie ~ Redefluss + Attraktivität, data = bsp)')

You get an error like this:

Error in parser(text = "fit <- lm(Sympathie ~ Redefluss +
Attraktivität, data = bsp)") :

/tmp/RtmpRU7Qf5/file16ff6a548215:1:45
unexpected input
> sessionInfo()
R version 2.14.2 (2012-02-29)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)

locale:
[1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C
[3] LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8 LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8
[5] LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8
[7] LC_PAPER=C LC_NAME=C
[9] LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C
[11] LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

attached base packages:
[1] stats graphics grDevices utils datasets methods base

[1] RCurl_1.91-1 tools_2.14.2


I cc the parser author to see if he has any solutions.

On knitr's side, you have to turn off highlighting, e.g.

<<tidy=FALSE, highlight=FALSE>>=

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Phone: 515-294-2465 Web: http://yihui.name
Department of Statistics, Iowa State University
2215 Snedecor Hall, Ames, IA
